title: Crisis in Yemen: "Imperative that World Powers Resolutely Defend International Maritime Law"
desc: All signs are pointing toward an escalation. UN Special Envoy to Yemen Hans Grundberg explains how close the two parties once were to peace - and what the prospects look like now.

title: Leaving the US: The Erosion of My American Dream
desc: After more than 30 years as a DER SPIEGEL correspondent in the US, I am leaving. The country that I thought I knew no longer exists. It was an illusion - and it is being replaced by the unknown.

title: Three Years of the Gaza War through the Eyes of Soldiers: "The Rule Was: 'Shoot Everyone You See'"
desc: More than 70,000 killed; even more wounded; destruction without end: Ten Israeli soldiers speak about feelings of revenge, orders to shoot and “collateral damage.”

title: "Exploited State Secrets for Profit": German Intelligence Rocked by Espionage Arrest of Former Chief
desc: The arrest of ex-BND chief August Hanning has sent shockwaves through the intelligence world. Yet Hanning’s dubious consulting work was no secret. Does German intelligence have a systemic problem?

title: Abuse in France: "Is Anyone Thinking of the Children?"
desc: France has been rocked by a wave of child abuse allegations directed at preschool caregivers. The scandal strikes at the heart of the country’s famed school system. Parents are furious.

title: Putin's War of Aggression: A Journey Along the Dnipro in Wartime Ukraine
desc: The mighty Dnipro slices right through Ukraine and - in the south - through the battlefield. A trip from north to south offers a unique perspective on how Ukrainians are surviving this war.
